title: WebSocket connection trace event state
description: Shape of the `state` field for WebSocket trace events: the endpoint and its transport, the handshake header lines, the open connections, the endpoint objects serving them, the frames on the wire and what the run cost.

url.description: The endpoint URL, ws:// or wss:// (e.g. 'ws://chat.example.com/ws/chat').

model.description: Technical code for how the container decides which object handles a connection; null on the comparison event.

endpointClass.description: The endpoint / handler class name, as the example named it.

allowedOrigin.description: The Origin the handshake is restricted to, or null when the server checks nothing.

transport.description: What the frames actually travel on.

protocol.description: Always TCP — a WebSocket has no UDP mode.

tls.description: True when TLS sits between TCP and the frames.

handshake.description: The last upgrade attempt, as header lines.

request.description: The HTTP GET the browser sent, line by line.

response.description: What the server answered: 101 Switching Protocols, or an ordinary error.

accepted.description: True after a 101, false after a refusal, null while the request is in flight.

connections.description: One entry per browser tab that has attempted a handshake.

phase.description: HTTP while still handshaking, OPEN once upgraded, CLOSED afterwards.

instance.description: The endpoint object serving this connection.

closeCode.description: The close status: 1000 normal, 1001 going away, 1006 abnormal (never on the wire).

instances.description: The endpoint objects the container created: one per connection, or one for all of them.

alive.description: False once its connection closed and it became garbage.

serves.description: The connections currently handled by this object.

fields.description: Instance fields written by handler code, and who wrote each one.

owner.description: The connection whose message wrote this value — the tell for a shared object.

frames.description: Every frame written since the upgrade, in order.

dir.description: IN is client to server, OUT is server to client.

opcode.description: The frame opcode: TEXT 0x1, BINARY 0x2, CLOSE 0x8, PING 0x9, PONG 0xA.

payload.description: What it carried, in the example's own words.

masked.description: True on client-to-server frames, which RFC 6455 requires to be masked.

bytes.description: Header plus masking key plus payload.

stats.description: Running totals for the whole run.

rejected.description: Handshakes refused with an ordinary HTTP error.

bytes.description: Total framed bytes in both directions.

clashes.description: Writes that overwrote another connection's value on a shared object.

leaks.description: Reads that returned another connection's value.

lost.description: Frames written into a socket that was no longer open.

closed.description: Connections ended by a close handshake.

dropped.description: Connections that died without a CLOSE frame (1006).

comparison.description: Only on INSTANCING_COMPARED: three connections priced through each instancing choice.

instances.description: Endpoint objects created for three connections.

fieldPerConnection.description: Whether an instance field belongs to one client.

needsSync.description: Whether mutable state inside the object must be thread-safe.

stateLives.description: Where per-connection state may safely be kept in this model.
